9: /// ## What it does
10: /// Checks for `for` loops that can be replaced with `yield from` expressions.
11: ///
12: /// ## Why is this bad?
13: /// If a `for` loop only contains a `yield` statement, it can be replaced with a
14: /// `yield from` expression, which is more concise and idiomatic.
15: ///
16: /// ## Example
17: /// ```python
18: /// for x in foo:
19: ///     yield x
20: /// ```
21: ///
22: /// Use instead:
23: /// ```python
24: /// yield from foo
25: /// ```
26: ///
27: /// ## Fix safety
28: /// This rule's fix is marked as unsafe, as converting a `for` loop to a `yield
29: /// from` expression can change the behavior of the program in rare cases.
30: /// For example, if a generator is being sent values via `send`, then rewriting
31: /// to a `yield from` could lead to an attribute error if the underlying
32: /// generator does not implement the `send` method.
33: ///
34: /// In most cases, however, the fix is safe, and such a modification should have
35: /// no effect on the behavior of the program.
36: ///
37: /// ## References
38: /// - [Python documentation: The `yield` statement](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/simple_stmts.html#the-yield-statement)
39: /// - [PEP 380 – Syntax for Delegating to a Subgenerator](https://peps.python.org/pep-0380/)
40: #[derive(ViolationMetadata)]
41: pub(crate) struct YieldInForLoop;
42: 
43: impl AlwaysFixableViolation for YieldInForLoop {
44:     #[derive_message_formats]
45:     fn message(&self) -> String {
46:         "Replace `yield` over `for` loop with `yield from`".to_string()
47:     }
48: 
49:     fn fix_title(&self) -> String {
50:         "Replace with `yield from`".to_string()
51:     }
52: }
53: 
54: /// Rewrite a `for` loop that solely yields its target into a `yield from`.
55: pub(crate) struct YieldFromRewrite<'a> {
56:     stmt_for: &'a ast::StmtFor,
57: }
58: 
59: impl<'a> YieldFromRewrite<'a> {
60:     pub(crate) fn new(stmt_for: &'a ast::StmtFor) -> Self {
61:         Self { stmt_for }
62:     }
63: 
64:     /// UP028
65:     pub(crate) fn yield_in_for_loop(&self, checker: &mut Checker) {
66:         // Intentionally omit async contexts.
67:         if in_async_context(checker) {
68:             return;
69:         }
70: 
71:         let stmt_for = self.stmt_for;
72: 
73:         // If there is an else statement, don't rewrite.
74:         if !stmt_for.orelse.is_empty() {
75:             return;
76:         }
77: 
78:         // If there's any logic besides a yield, don't rewrite.
79:         let [body] = stmt_for.body.as_slice() else {
80:             return;
81:         };
82: 
83:         let Some(value) = yielded_value(body) else {
84:             return;
85:         };
86: 
87:         // If the target is not the same as the value, don't rewrite. For example, we should rewrite
88:         // `for x in y: yield x` to `yield from y`, but not `for x in y: yield x + 1`.
89:         if !is_same_expr(&stmt_for.target, value) {
90:             return;
91:         }
92: 
93:         // If any of the bound names are used outside of the yield itself, don't rewrite.
94:         if collect_names(value).any(|name| name_escapes_yield(checker, name)) {
95:             return;
96:         }
97: 
98:         let mut diagnostic = Diagnostic::new(YieldInForLoop, stmt_for.range());
99:         let locator = checker.locator();
100:         let indexer = checker.indexer();
101:         let iter = stmt_for.iter.as_ref();
102:         let contents = locator.slice(
103:             parenthesized_range(
104:                 iter.into(),
105:                 stmt_for.into(),
106:                 indexer.comment_ranges(),
107:                 locator.contents(),
108:             )
109:             .unwrap_or(iter.range()),
110:         );
111:         let contents = format!("yield from {contents}");
112:         diagnostic.set_fix(Fix::unsafe_edit(Edit::range_replacement(
113:             contents,
114:             diagnostic.range,
115:         )));
116:         checker.diagnostics.push(diagnostic);
117:     }
118: }
119: 
120: fn in_async_context(checker: &Checker) -> bool {
121:     checker.semantic().in_async_context()
122: }
123: 
124: fn yielded_value(body: &Stmt) -> Option<&Expr> {
125:     let Stmt::Expr(ast::StmtExpr { value, range: _ }) = body else {
126:         return None;
127:     };
128:     let Expr::Yield(ast::ExprYield {
129:         value: Some(value),
130:         range: _,
131:     }) = value.as_ref()
132:     else {
133:         return None;
134:     };
135:     Some(value)
136: }
137: 
138: fn name_escapes_yield(checker: &Checker, name: &ast::ExprName) -> bool {
139:     checker
140:         .semantic()
141:         .current_scope()
142:         .get_all(name.id.as_str())
143:         // Skip unbound bindings like `del x`
144:         .find(|&id| !checker.semantic().binding(id).is_unbound())
145:         .is_some_and(|binding_id| {
146:             let binding = checker.semantic().binding(binding_id);
147:             binding.references.iter().any(|reference_id| {
148:                 checker.semantic().reference(*reference_id).range() != name.range()
149:             })
150:         })
151: }
152: 
153: /// Return `true` if the two expressions are equivalent, and both consistent solely
154: /// of tuples and names.
155: fn is_same_expr(left: &Expr, right: &Expr) -> bool {
156:     match (&left, &right) {
157:         (Expr::Name(left), Expr::Name(right)) => left.id == right.id,
158:         (Expr::Tuple(left), Expr::Tuple(right)) => {
159:             left.len() == right.len()
160:                 && left
161:                     .iter()
162:                     .zip(right)
163:                     .all(|(left, right)| is_same_expr(left, right))
164:         }
165:         _ => false,
166:     }
167: }
168: 
169: /// Collect all named variables in an expression consisting solely of tuples and
170: /// names.
171: fn collect_names<'a>(expr: &'a Expr) -> Box<dyn Iterator<Item = &'a ast::ExprName> + 'a> {
172:     Box::new(
173:         expr.as_name_expr().into_iter().chain(
174:             expr.as_tuple_expr()
175:                 .into_iter()
176:                 .flat_map(|tuple| tuple.iter().flat_map(collect_names)),
177:         ),
178:     )
179: }
